summary:
**Conversation overview:**

The person asked Claude to conduct a comprehensive survey of web games and projects built with Claude Fable 5.1/5.2 (single-file HTML/CSS/JS applications), mentioning examples like shooter games and a Van Gogh painting exploration game, with the goal of building a complete database including all available GitHub repositories. Claude executed this through extensive web searches, cloned 73 GitHub repositories (including 5 aggregator/awesome-list repos), fetched data from multiple community showcase sites (fable52.games with 42 games, ai8games.com with 62 games, a demo gallery with 62 entries, sorrycc/fable-arcade with 8 Fable 5.1 games, and Anil-matcha's awesome-claude-fable-5-1 list with 88 use-case entries), and merged everything into a deduplicated database. The final deliverable was a SQLite database with two tables (543 projects, 73 repos), accompanying CSV/JSON exports, a repo manifest with file-type statistics and README summaries, a compressed source-code snapshot (split into three parts due to size limits), and a clone_all.sh script for retrieving full repositories. Claude documented known limitations including: 59 of 543 project records have linked repos while 273 have live demo links; most showcased works only exist as video posts on X without accessible source; repo categorization (project/aggregator/tool_or_skill/film_animation/web_or_tool/unrelated_preexisting) was done by manual README inspection; GitHub's search API was unavailable without an authenticated account, so repo discovery relied on web search, GitHub topic pages, and community lists; and some topic-page repos claiming to offer "free desktop Fable" were excluded as unrelated and potentially risky. The person did not provide corrections during this conversation; Claude proactively sent progress updates mid-task and offered to produce a Neo4j-importable knowledge-graph format as a next step if the person wants relationships between authors, model versions, tech stacks, and repos mapped out.

**Tool knowledge:**

GitHub's `gh search repos` and `gh auth status` require an authenticated account and were not available in this environment; public repo discovery had to rely on `git clone` (which works without auth), web search, and WebFetch against GitHub topic pages like `github.com/topics/fable-5-2` and `github.com/topics/claude-fable` to enumerate tagged repositories. When cloning many repos in bulk, parallelizing with `xargs -P 6` and `--depth 1 --timeout 90` per clone was effective for handling dozens of repos without excessive wait time. For deriving additional repo candidates beyond known lists, parsing GitHub Pages URLs (pattern `https://{user}.github.io/{repo}`) out of an existing structured dataset (a `works.json` aggregator file) via regex successfully surfaced repos not found through direct search. When building deliverable files for SendUserFile, output size matters: a 63.6 MiB tar.gz exceeded the upload limit, requiring `split -b 25m` into numbered parts (verified identical via `cmp` after `cat`-ing parts back together) with instructions for the person to reassemble using `cat part* > file`. For SQLite + JSON dual-output builds, writing JSON with `ensure_ascii=False` is necessary to preserve non-ASCII (e.g., Chinese) titles correctly rather than escaping them. When deduplicating records from multiple sources (URL, repo URL, title), normalizing URLs by stripping protocol/www/trailing-slash and normalizing titles by removing non-alphanumeric characters before matching was necessary to catch cross-source duplicates that differed only in formatting.
